quests.instruction: You spot shiny berries on a bush during a walk. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a grown-up who knows plants before eating any
options: Taste one berry first to check if it is safe
Ask a grown-up who knows plants before eating any
Pick them all and eat them if they look nice
quests.hint: Some wild berries are not safe, so check first.
quests.explanation: Some wild berries are harmless, but others can make you very sick, so only eat wild fruit that a grown-up who knows plants says is safe.
quests.funFact: Experts learn to tell plants apart by their leaves, flowers and fruit, not just the berries.

quests.instruction: At a pick-your-own fruit farm, which is a good rule?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick only ripe fruit and place it gently in a basket
options: Pick every fruit and drop it on the ground
Pick only ripe fruit and place it gently in a basket
Taste a bite of every fruit and put it back
quests.hint: Think about what is fair to the farmer and good for the fruit.
quests.explanation: Picking only ripe fruit and handling it gently keeps the fruit from being wasted or bruised.
quests.funFact: At pick-your-own farms, the fruit is often weighed afterwards so you pay for what you pick.

quests.instruction: Why are berry bushes sometimes covered with nets?
quests.correctAnswer: To keep birds from eating the fruit
options: To make the berries grow bigger
To keep the berries warm at night
To keep birds from eating the fruit
quests.hint: Think about who else loves ripe berries.
quests.explanation: Nets keep hungry birds away from the ripe berries so more fruit is left for people.
quests.funFact: The nets are light enough to let sunshine and rain through to the plants.

quests.instruction: Many apple trees make more fruit when a different apple variety grows nearby. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: Bees carry pollen between the different trees
options: The two kinds of trees share the same roots
The two kinds of trees keep each other warm
Bees carry pollen between the different trees
quests.hint: Think about who visits blossoms.
quests.explanation: Many apple varieties need pollen from a different variety, and bees carry it from tree to tree.
quests.funFact: Orchards often plant a few pollen-sharing trees among the main rows.

quests.instruction: Which animals visit durian flowers at night and carry pollen?
quests.correctAnswer: Bats
options: Bats
Butterflies
Ladybugs
quests.hint: Durian flowers open in the evening.
quests.explanation: Durian flowers open at night, and bats visit them and carry pollen from flower to flower.
quests.funFact: Durian flowers last only a short time before they fall.

quests.instruction: On many date farms, workers dab pollen onto flowers by hand. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: To make sure more flowers turn into dates
options: To make the dates sweeter and darker
To scare birds away from the flowers
To make sure more flowers turn into dates
quests.hint: Think about what pollen does for a flower.
quests.explanation: Hand pollination makes sure more date flowers receive pollen, so more of them turn into fruit.
quests.funFact: Date palms are either male or female, and only the female trees make dates.

quests.instruction: What is the big benefit of a dwarf fruit tree?
quests.correctAnswer: It stays small, so the fruit is easy to reach
options: It grows its fruit underground, safe from birds
It stays small, so the fruit is easy to reach
It needs no sunlight, so it can grow indoors
quests.hint: Think about picking fruit without a tall ladder.
quests.explanation: Dwarf fruit trees stay small, so pruning and picking are easier and safer.
quests.funFact: Some dwarf apple trees are only about as tall as a person.

quests.instruction: Which fruit tree is often grown in a pot so it can be moved indoors when it gets cold?
quests.correctAnswer: Lemon
options: Lemon
Coconut
Jackfruit
quests.hint: Think of a citrus tree that stays fairly small.
quests.explanation: Lemon trees can grow in big pots and be moved inside when it gets cold. Coconut palms and jackfruit trees grow far too large for pots.
quests.funFact: Small lemon trees can give fruit on a sunny balcony or patio.

quests.instruction: A baby plant that has just sprouted from a seed is called what?
quests.correctAnswer: A seedling
options: A seedling
A segment
A shell
quests.hint: It is tiny and green.
quests.explanation: A seedling is a young plant that has just sprouted from a seed.
quests.funFact: A seedling lives on food stored inside its seed until its leaves can make food.

quests.instruction: Lychee and many citrus trees grow in subtropical places. What does subtropical mean?
quests.correctAnswer: Warm, with a short cooler season
options: Freezing cold for most of the year
Warm, with a short cooler season
Hot and dry with no rain at all
quests.hint: Think of a place next to the tropics.
quests.explanation: Subtropical places are warm for most of the year and have only a short, mild cool season.
quests.funFact: Subtropical places often have mild winters with little or no snow.

quests.instruction: Which fruit needs hot, humid weather close to the equator all year?
quests.correctAnswer: Mangosteen
options: Mangosteen
Cherries
Apple
quests.hint: Think of a tree that never gets a cold winter.
quests.explanation: Mangosteen trees need constant warmth and moisture. Cherries and apples need a cool winter.
quests.funFact: Mangosteen trees grow slowly and may take around ten years to give their first fruit.

quests.instruction: Places with warm summers and cool winters are called temperate. Which fruit grows well there?
quests.correctAnswer: Pear
options: Durian
Mangosteen
Pear
quests.hint: Think about fruit trees that rest in winter.
quests.explanation: Pear trees grow well in temperate places. Durian and mangosteen need warmth all year.
quests.funFact: Temperate places usually have four clear seasons.

quests.instruction: After a flower is pollinated, which part grows into the fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: The center of the flower, where the seeds start
options: The colorful petals that surround the center
The center of the flower, where the seeds start
The roots under the plant that fed the flower
quests.hint: Petals usually fall off, but something stays behind.
quests.explanation: After pollination, the part in the center of the flower swells and becomes the fruit, while the petals usually fall away.
quests.funFact: You can often see tiny baby fruits behind fading blossoms.

quests.instruction: Why do growers sometimes prop up the branches of a tree full of fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: To stop heavy branches from snapping
options: To make the fruit grow bigger and faster
To keep the tree's roots cool in summer
To stop heavy branches from snapping
quests.hint: Think about how heavy a branch of fruit can get.
quests.explanation: A big harvest can make branches heavy enough to bend or break, so props help hold them up.
quests.funFact: A big harvest can bend branches almost down to the ground.

quests.instruction: Why are many fruits colorful and sweet?
quests.correctAnswer: To attract animals that spread their seeds
options: To attract animals that spread their seeds
To hide from bees that want to eat them
To keep rain from soaking into the fruit
quests.hint: Think about what an animal does after eating fruit.
quests.explanation: Bright colors and sweet flavors attract animals that eat the fruit and carry the seeds to new places.
quests.funFact: Birds see colors well, which is one reason many berries they eat are red or blue.

quests.instruction: A peach is picked on a farm, packed in a tray and sold in a shop. Which step comes first?
quests.correctAnswer: Picking it from the tree
options: Picking it from the tree
Selling it in the shop
Packing it in a tray
quests.hint: Think about where the peach starts.
quests.explanation: The peach is picked first, then packed, and finally sold in the shop.
quests.funFact: Fruit is often picked in the cool early morning.

quests.instruction: Why are some fruits picked before they are fully ripe?
quests.correctAnswer: So they stay firm during the trip to the shop
options: So they taste more sour when they arrive
So they stay firm during the trip to the shop
So they can be turned into juice at the shop
quests.hint: Think about how a long trip can squash soft fruit.
quests.explanation: Firm, not-yet-ripe fruit handles bumps and long trips better, and many fruits finish ripening later.
quests.funFact: Some fruits keep ripening after they are picked, but others stop.

quests.instruction: Why are many fruits kept cool while they travel from farm to shop?
quests.correctAnswer: To keep them fresh for longer
options: To make them taste more sour
To keep them fresh for longer
To turn them into juice slowly
quests.hint: Think about what warmth does to soft fruit.
quests.explanation: Cool temperatures slow down ripening and spoiling, so fruit stays fresh for longer.
quests.funFact: Some fruit travels across oceans in cooled shipping containers.

quests.instruction: Trees that drop all their leaves in autumn are called what?
quests.correctAnswer: Deciduous
options: Deciduous
Evergreen
Tropical
quests.hint: Think of bare branches in winter.
quests.explanation: Deciduous trees, like apple and cherry trees, drop their leaves in autumn. Evergreen trees keep theirs.
quests.funFact: The leaves of many deciduous trees turn red, orange or yellow before they fall.

quests.instruction: What do we call it when a tree rests in winter and stops growing for a while?
quests.correctAnswer: Dormancy
options: Pollination
Dormancy
Irrigation
quests.hint: Think of a tree taking a long nap.
quests.explanation: Dormancy is a resting time when a tree slows down, which helps many fruit trees flower well in spring.
quests.funFact: A dormant tree looks bare, but it is alive and resting.

quests.instruction: Heavy rain just before harvest can make some ripe cherries split. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: They soak up too much water
options: They get too hot in the sun
They run out of sugar inside
They soak up too much water
quests.hint: Think about what happens when something is filled too full.
quests.explanation: Cherries can soak up extra water through their skin until they burst open.
quests.funFact: Growers sometimes cover cherry trees to protect the fruit from rain.

quests.instruction: Why are banana plants sometimes propped up with poles?
quests.correctAnswer: Heavy bunches can topple the tall, soft stem
options: The poles help the bananas ripen faster
The poles keep new leaves from growing
Heavy bunches can topple the tall, soft stem
quests.hint: Think about the weight of a full bunch.
quests.explanation: A full bunch is heavy, and a banana stem is soft rather than woody, so poles stop plants from toppling over in wind.
quests.funFact: Banana plants have huge leaves that can be two meters long.

quests.instruction: Why do some melon growers set a board or straw under each melon?
quests.correctAnswer: To keep it off wet soil so it does not rot
options: To keep it off wet soil so it does not rot
To make the melon's stripes grow darker
To stop the vine from climbing upward
quests.hint: Think about what damp soil does to fruit.
quests.explanation: Melons rest on the ground, and wet soil can make them rot or get spots, so a board or straw keeps them dry and clean.
quests.funFact: Straw also helps keep weeds down around the vines.

quests.instruction: Which of these grows on a bushy plant that is often tied to a stake?
quests.correctAnswer: Tomato
options: Tomato
Mango
Coconut
quests.hint: The others grow on tall trees.
quests.explanation: Tomato plants are bushy or vining and are often tied to stakes. Mango and coconut grow on tall trees.
quests.funFact: Tomato plants can keep giving fruit all summer in warm weather.

quests.instruction: How can a garden help bees, which pollinate fruit trees?
quests.correctAnswer: Plant flowers they like
options: Remove all the flowers
Plant flowers they like
Cover the garden with plastic
quests.hint: Think about what bees visit.
quests.explanation: Bees visit flowers for nectar, so planting flowers gives them food and helps fruit trees get pollinated.
quests.funFact: A mix of different flowers gives bees food for more of the year.

quests.instruction: Why is it good to eat the fruit we pick or buy instead of wasting it?
quests.correctAnswer: Growing fruit takes time, water and work
options: Fruit grows by itself in just minutes
Fruit does not need any sunshine or water
Growing fruit takes time, water and work
quests.hint: Remember everything a fruit plant needs to grow.
quests.explanation: Fruit needs sun, water, care and time to grow, so it is good not to waste it.
quests.funFact: Overripe fruit can be blended into smoothies or baked into bread.

quests.instruction: Besides fruit, what can a fruit tree give us?
quests.correctAnswer: Shade and a home for birds
options: Extra rain and a cooler climate
Shade and a home for birds
Bright sunshine and warm nights
quests.hint: Think about what a big tree offers.
quests.explanation: A fruit tree gives shade and can be a home for birds and insects as well as fruit.
quests.funFact: Blossoming fruit trees also give bees a lot of food in spring.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both grow on climbing vines?
quests.correctAnswer: Grapes and kiwi
options: Grapes and kiwi
Apples and pears
Mangoes and papayas
quests.hint: Think about tendrils and trellises.
quests.explanation: Grapes and kiwi grow on climbing vines. Apples and pears grow on trees, and mangoes and papayas grow in warm places on tall plants.
quests.funFact: Both grape and kiwi vines need strong supports to climb.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both grow best in the warm tropics?
quests.correctAnswer: Pineapples and papayas
options: Apples and cherries
Cranberries and blueberries
Pineapples and papayas
quests.hint: Think about fruits that need warmth all year.
quests.explanation: Pineapples and papayas need warm weather all year. Apples and cherries prefer cool winters, and cranberries and blueberries like cooler places.
quests.funFact: The tropics get plenty of sunshine and warmth for growing fruit all year.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both grow on low plants?
quests.correctAnswer: Strawberries and pineapples
options: Cherries and apricot trees
Mangoes and coconut palms
Strawberries and pineapples
quests.hint: Think about fruits that grow close to the soil.
quests.explanation: Strawberries and pineapples grow on low plants. Cherries, apricots, mangoes and coconuts grow on trees.
quests.funFact: Both strawberries and pineapples can be grown from parts of the parent plant.
